questions.question: In March 2025, which anniversary of National Defence Day was observed to honour the sacrifices of India’s armed forces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**87th Anniversary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **National Defence Day **is observed annually in India to** honor the sacrifices and contributions of the armed forces** in safeguarding the nation's security and sovereignty.
 
• The year 2025 marked the **87th anniversary** of National Defence Day, which traces its roots back to significant military events in **1938**.
 
• This day is dedicated to recognizing the valor, dedication, and commitment of personnel from the **Army, Navy, and Air Force**.
 
• National Defence Day also serves as a platform to spread awareness about the importance of a robust defense system in maintaining peace and security.
 
• Various ceremonies, parades, and tributes are organized across the country to commemorate the occasion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Armed Forces**

 
 
• India's armed forces consist of three main branches: the Army, Navy, and Air Force, along with auxiliary organizations like the Coast Guard.
 
• The **President **of India serves as the **Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• India has one of the largest and most powerful military forces in the world, with a focus on modernization and self-reliance in defense production.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The establishment of National Defence Day is tied to key milestones in India's military history, including contributions during pre-independence and post-independence periods.
 
• It is a day to remember the martyrs who laid down their lives in service to the nation.
 
 
 
• **Important Military Operations**
 
 
• India's armed forces have participated in several notable operations, including the** Indo-Pak Wars (1947, 1965, 1971, and 1999)**, the **Sino-Indian War (1962)**, and peacekeeping missions under the United Nations.
 
• They play a crucial role in disaster relief, internal security, and maintaining strategic stability in the region.
 
 
 
• **Key Military Institutions**
 
 
• India has premier institutions like the** National Defence Academy (NDA), Indian Military Academy (IMA), and Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** to train and equip its armed forces.
 
• These institutions contribute significantly to the development of military strategies, technology, and leadership.

questions.question: In February 2025, five cheetahs were released into which national park of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuno National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In February 2025, five cheetahs were released into **Kuno National Park**, located in **Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• This release is part of India's ambitious **Cheetah Reintroduction Project**, aimed at reintroducing cheetahs in the country after their extinction nearly 70 years ago.
 
• The cheetahs were translocated from Africa as part of a collaborative effort between India and countries like **Namibia and South Africa**.
 
• Kuno National Park was selected for this project due to its suitable habitat, abundant prey base, and minimal human-wildlife conflict.
 
• This effort is a step toward restoring ecological balance and ensuring the conservation of endangered species in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuno National Park**

 
 
• Located in the **Sheopur district of Madhya Pradesh**, Kuno was declared a national park in **2018**.
 
• The park spans over an area of approximately 748 square kilometers and is known for its diverse flora and fauna.
 
• Kuno was originally considered a potential site for relocating Asiatic lions from Gir National Park in Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **Cheetah Reintroduction in India**
 
 
• **Cheetahs were declared extinct in India in 1952 due to habitat loss**, hunting, and human interference.
 
• The current reintroduction plan is the first time wild cheetahs have been translocated across continents.
 
• The project involves collaborative efforts with Namibia and South Africa, where the cheetahs were sourced.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance of Cheetahs**
 
 
• Cheetahs are apex predators, playing a critical role in maintaining the balance of ecosystems.
 
• Their presence helps control herbivore populations, promoting the growth of vegetation and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of the Project**
 
 
• Ensuring the survival and adaptation of cheetahs to their new environment is a significant challenge.
 
• Potential risks include poaching, human-wildlife conflict, and insufficient prey base in the area.
 
• Continuous monitoring, habitat management, and public awareness are crucial for the project's success.

questions.question: On 24 January 2025, which day was celebrated to promote girls’ rights and welfare in India?

• **National Girl Child Day **is celebrated in India every year on **24th January** to promote awareness about the rights, education, and health of girl children.
 
• It was first initiated by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** in 2008 to highlight the issues faced by girls in India and to empower them.
 
• The day emphasizes addressing **gender-based discrimination** and promoting gender equality in all aspects of society.
 
• Various campaigns and events are organized across the country to spread awareness about the importance of saving, educating, and empowering the girl child.
 
• The celebration aligns with the goals of government schemes like **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**, which focuses on improving the welfare and status of girls in India.

• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP):**

 
 
• Launched in 2015, it aims to address declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)** and promote the survival, protection, and education of the girl child.
 
• The campaign is a tri-ministerial effort involving the Ministries of Women and Child Development, Health and Family Welfare, and Education.
 
 
 
• **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY):**
 
 
• A government-backed savings scheme aimed at securing the future of girl children.

• **Gender Inequality in India:**

• Promoting girl child education and empowerment is pivotal to achieving societal progress and economic development.
 
 
 
• **United Nations International Day of the Girl Child:**
 
 
• Celebrated globally on **11th October**, it complements India's National Girl Child Day by advocating for girls' rights worldwide.
 
• The focus is on issues like education, healthcare access, and ending child marriage.

questions.question: Agro-forestry was conceived on the recommendation of which policy to promote plantation on farmlands?

options.text: Protection of Plant Varieties & Farmers' Rights Act, 2001

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Agro-forestry Policy, 2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Agro-forestry Policy, 2014** was introduced by the Government of India to promote agro-forestry practices across the country.
 
• This policy aims to integrate **trees and agriculture on farmland**, enhancing productivity, livelihoods, and environmental sustainability.
 
• The policy encourages farmers to grow trees alongside crops on their farmland, ensuring a balance between agricultural and forestry practices.
 
• It emphasizes the **relaxation of regulatory constraints** related to tree felling, transportation, and marketing of agro-forestry produce.
 
• The National Agro-forestry Policy, 2014, aligns with India's commitments to increasing forest cover and promoting sustainable agricultural practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agro-forestry:**

 
 
• Agro-forestry is a land-use system that integrates trees and shrubs with crops and livestock on the same land.
 
• It helps in improving **soil fertility, water retention, and biodiversity** while also providing economic benefits to farmers.
 
• Common agro-forestry practices include alley cropping, silvopasture, and windbreaks.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Agro-forestry:**
 
 
• It enhances carbon sequestration, contributing to climate change mitigation.
 
• Agro-forestry reduces soil erosion and improves soil health, ensuring sustainable farming practices.
 
• It provides additional income through timber, fruits, and other forest-based products.
 
 
 
• **National Forest Policy, 1988:**
 
 
• The National Forest Policy of 1988 emphasizes **maintaining ecological balance and preserving biodiversity**.
 
• The policy aims to** increase forest and tree cover to 33% of India's geographical area**.
 
 
 
• **India's Agro-forestry Mission:**
 
 
• The** National Agro-forestry Policy, 2014**, is implemented under the ambit of the **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare**.
 
• It aligns with India's **National Action Plan on Climate Change** and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

questions.question: How many launches of the LVM-3 rocket are planned for the Chandrayaan-4 mission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Chandrayaan-4 **mission by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is planned to have **two launches using the LVM-3 rocket**.
 
• The **LVM-3** (Launch Vehicle Mark-3) is ISRO's heaviest and most advanced launch vehicle, capable of carrying **payloads up to 8,000 kg to Low Earth Orbit **(LEO).
 
• The two launches will ensure the deployment of the required mission components, which may include an orbiter, lander, and rover, depending on the mission design.
 
• The Chandrayaan-4 mission is expected to build on the advancements made during the Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 missions, focusing on lunar exploration and scientific research.
 
• ISRO uses the LVM-3 rocket for critical missions due to its high reliability and capability to handle complex payloads.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **LVM-3 Rocket (Launch Vehicle Mark-3):**

 
 
• The LVM-3, previously known as **GSLV Mk-III**, is a three-stage heavy-lift launch vehicle developed by ISRO.
 
• It has a lift-off mass of approximately 640 tons and stands 43.5 meters tall.
 
• The rocket uses a combination of solid, liquid, and cryogenic propulsion systems.
 
• LVM-3 is also the launch vehicle for India’s human spaceflight program, Gaganyaan.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan Missions:**
 
 
• Chandrayaan-1 (2008): India’s first lunar mission focused on mapping the Moon’s surface and detecting water molecules.
 
• Chandrayaan-2 (2019): Aimed at soft-landing a rover on the lunar south pole, though the lander lost communication during descent.
 
• Chandrayaan-3 (2023): Successfully demonstrated soft-landing and deployed a rover for lunar surface exploration.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Objectives of Chandrayaan-4:**
 
 
• To further explore the lunar surface, particularly the unexplored south pole region.
 
• To conduct advanced experiments on lunar geology, topography, and surface composition.
 
• To test new technologies for future interplanetary missions.
 
 
 
• **ISRO's Lunar Exploration Roadmap:**
 
 
• ISRO plans to establish a strong presence in lunar exploration as part of its long-term goals.
 
• Future missions include more advanced lunar landers and potential collaboration with international space agencies.

questions.question: In the context of computer memory hierarchy, which of the following statements regarding access speed and cost per bit is generally true as you move from registers towards secondary storage?

options.text: Access speed increases and cost per bit decreases
Access speed increases and cost per bit increases
Access speed decreases and cost per bit decreases
Access speed decreases and cost per bit increases.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Access speed decreases and cost per bit decreases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As we move down the memory hierarchy—from registers to secondary storage—the **access speed decreases**. Registers are the fastest, while secondary storage devices like hard drives are significantly slower.
 
• The **cost per bit of storage decreases** as we move from registers to secondary storage. Registers and cache are expensive due to their high-speed performance and small size.
 
• Registers are located within the CPU, offering **nanosecond-level access times**, whereas secondary storage devices like HDDs or SSDs have access times in milliseconds or microseconds.
 
• Secondary storage devices, such as hard drives, offer **much larger storage capacity** at a lower cost per bit but are slower in terms of data retrieval compared to primary memory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Memory Hierarchy in Computers**

 
 
• It refers to the arrangement of memory types based on **speed, cost, and capacity**.
 
• It typically includes registers, cache, main memory (RAM), and secondary storage (HDD/SSD).
 
• Registers and cache are the fastest but have the smallest capacity, while secondary storage is slower but offers large capacity.
 
 
 
• **Access Time**
 
 
• Access time is the time taken by the CPU to retrieve data from memory.
 
• Registers have the shortest access time, measured in nanoseconds, while secondary storage access time is measured in milliseconds or microseconds.
 
 
 
• **Cost per Bit**
 
 
• Cost per bit refers to the expense incurred for storing one bit of data.
 
• Registers and cache have the highest cost per bit, while secondary storage devices have the lowest cost per bit.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Storage**
 
 
• Includes devices like HDDs, SSDs, and optical disks.
 
• It is non-volatile and provides persistent storage for data even when the system is powered off.
 
 
 
• **Registers**
 
 
• Smallest and fastest memory located directly within the CPU.
 
• Used to temporarily store data that is actively being processed by the CPU.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in Part IV of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Promotion of international peace and security
Promotion of Hindi language as a medium of expression
Provision for free and compulsory education for children
Organisation of agricultural and animal husbandry

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Promotion of Hindi language as a medium of expression**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which provides guidelines for the establishment of a just society.
 
• The promotion of Hindi language as a medium of expression is not explicitly mentioned in Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• Article 51 of Part IV mentions the promotion of international peace and security as one of the Directive Principles.
 
• Other provisions under Part IV include the organisation of agricultural and animal husbandry (Article 48) and the provision for free and compulsory education for children (Article 45).
 
• The Directive Principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life, ensuring equality and welfare for all.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy:**

 
 
• Directive Principles are non-justiciable guidelines for governance provided to the State.
 
• These principles are inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to achieve socio-economic justice.
 
• They are categorized into economic and social, Gandhian, and international principles.
 
 
 
• **Article 51 (Promotion of International Peace):**
 
 
• The State shall promote international peace and security.
 
• It aims to maintain just and honorable relations between nations and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.
 
 
 
• **Article 45 (Education for Children):**
 
 
• The Constitution mandates free and compulsory education for children until they reach the age of 14 years.
 
• This was later reinforced by the Right to Education Act, 2009.
 
 
 
• **Article 48 (Agriculture and Animal Husbandry):**
 
 
• The State shall endeavor to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines.
 
• It also aims to preserve and improve breeds and prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle.
 
 
 
• **Promotion of Hindi Language:**
 
 
• Provisions related to the promotion of Hindi language are covered under Part XVII (Articles 343-351) of the Constitution.
 
• It emphasizes the development of Hindi as the official language and its enrichment by assimilating elements from other Indian languages.

questions.question: In January 2025, National Youth Day was celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of which Indian leader?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Youth Day is celebrated annually on **12th January** to commemorate the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.
 
• The Government of India declared Swami Vivekananda's birthday as National Youth Day in **1984** to honor his contributions towards inspiring youth.
 
• Swami Vivekananda, a key figure in introducing Indian philosophies like Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world, believed in the power of youth for nation-building.
 
• His teachings focused on **self-confidence, self-reliance, and spirituality**, making him an ideal role model for Indian youth.
 
• Various programs, including speeches, seminars, cultural performances, and competitions, are organized across India on National Youth Day to spread awareness about his life and ideals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Vivekananda:**

 
 
• Born on **12th January 1863** in Kolkata, India, he was originally named Narendranath Datta.
 
• He was a disciple of **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa** and went on to establish the **Ramakrishna Mission** in 1897.
 
• Swami Vivekananda is best known for his speech at the **1893 Parliament of the World's Religions** in Chicago, where he introduced Hinduism to the global audience.
 
• His famous quote, "Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached," continues to inspire millions worldwide.
 
 
 
• **National Youth Day Themes:**
 
 
• Every year, National Youth Day is celebrated with a particular theme to engage the youth in constructive activities.
 
• The themes are centered around topics like **youth empowerment, innovation, and spirituality**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of National Youth Day:**
 
 
• The day serves to highlight the role of youth in shaping the future of the nation.
 
• It encourages young people to imbibe the teachings of Swami Vivekananda and work towards self-development and societal progress.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Swami Vivekananda's ideas on religious harmony, universal brotherhood, and the empowerment of youth resonate globally.
 
• His contributions to philosophy and spirituality have earned him recognition as one of India's greatest cultural ambassadors.

questions.question: Which of the following devices can function as both input and output devices?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Touch Screen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **touch screen** is an electronic display that can act as both an **input and output device**.
 
• As an input device, it allows users to interact with the system by touching the screen using a finger or stylus.
 
• As an output device, it displays visual content, such as text, images, or videos, similar to a regular screen or monitor.
 
• Touch screens are commonly used in smartphones, tablets, ATMs, interactive kiosks, and other digital devices.
 
• They employ various technologies such as resistive, capacitive, infrared, or surface acoustic wave to detect and process touch inputs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistive Touch Screen:**

 
 
• It uses two electrically conductive layers separated by a small gap.
 
• When pressure is applied to the screen, the layers come into contact, registering the touch input.
 
• Commonly used in older devices and ATM machines.
 
 
 
• **Capacitive Touch Screen:**
 
 
• It works by sensing the electrical conductivity of the user's finger.
 
• Capacitive screens are more responsive and support multi-touch gestures.
 
• They are widely used in smartphones and modern tablets.
 
 
 
• **Infrared Touch Screen:**
 
 
• This technology uses infrared light beams to detect touch.
 
• It does not require physical contact; even proximity can register input.
 
• Typically found in interactive kiosks and large touch displays.
 
 
 
• **Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) Touch Screen:**
 
 
• SAW screens rely on ultrasonic waves that pass over the touch screen surface.
 
• When the screen is touched, the waves are absorbed, allowing the location of the touch to be determined.
 
• They provide high clarity and durability but are sensitive to external contaminants.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Touch Screens:**
 
 
• Touch screens are widely used in **retail stores, healthcare, education, gaming, and industrial automation.**
 
• They enable intuitive user experiences, reducing the need for external peripherals like keyboards or mice.

questions.question: Which of the following changes was introduced in 2024 under the Companies Act amendments to enhance corporate social responsibility (CSR) transparency in India?

options.text: Exemption of companies with a turnover below ₹500 crore from CSR obligations
Reduction in the minimum CSR spending threshold for all eligible companies
Requirement for at least 50% of board members to be CSR specialists
Mandatory quarterly CSR reporting accompanied by independent audits

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandatory quarterly CSR reporting accompanied by independent audits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2024, the Indian government amended the Companies Act to improve **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) transparency**.
 
• The amendment introduced **mandatory quarterly CSR reporting** for eligible companies to ensure regular updates on CSR activities.
 
• Independent audits of the CSR reports were made **compulsory** to enhance credibility and accountability.
 
• The change aims to address issues of non-compliance, misuse of CSR funds, and ensure alignment of CSR activities with their intended social objectives.
 
• This step is part of broader efforts to encourage **responsible corporate governance** and increase trust among stakeholders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR):**

 
 
• CSR refers to the practices where businesses voluntarily contribute to sustainable development by delivering economic, social, and environmental benefits.
 
• In India, Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates CSR spending for companies meeting certain financial thresholds.
 
• Eligible companies must spend at least 2% of their average net profit of the last 3 years on CSR activities.
 
 
 
• **Independent Audits:**
 
 
• Independent audits involve third-party examination of financial or operational processes to ensure compliance and accuracy.
 
• In the context of CSR, these audits validate the effectiveness and alignment of CSR projects with prescribed norms.
 
 
 
• **CSR Reporting:**
 
 
• CSR reporting involves documenting and disclosing information about a company’s CSR activities, expenditures, and outcomes.
 
• Quarterly reporting ensures transparency and provides regular updates to stakeholders about the company’s contribution to social development.
 
 
 
• **Impact of CSR Amendments:**
 
 
• Improves corporate accountability and stakeholder confidence.
 
• Encourages companies to align their CSR initiatives with national development goals.
 
• Addresses misuse or underutilization of CSR funds by ensuring stricter compliance.

questions.question: In which state is the shifting agriculture known as ‘Jhum’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Jhum' is the local name for **shifting cultivation** practiced predominantly in the northeastern states of India, including Assam.
 
• It involves clearing a patch of forest land, burning the vegetation, and using the ash as fertilizer to grow crops.
 
• After cultivating the land for a few years, farmers leave it fallow to allow the soil to regain its fertility.
 
• Jhum cultivation is a traditional practice among tribal communities and is deeply rooted in their culture and livelihood.
 
• This agricultural method is also practiced in other northeastern states like Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Arunachal Pradesh, but Assam remains one of the prominent regions for Jhum cultivation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shifting Cultivation:** It is an agricultural practice where land is cultivated temporarily, then abandoned to allow natural vegetation to regenerate.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** Jhum cultivation has been criticized for causing deforestation, soil erosion, and loss of biodiversity in the northeastern states.
 
• **Sustainable Alternatives:** The Indian government and various NGOs promote sustainable agricultural practices like terrace farming as alternatives to Jhum cultivation.
 
• **Historical Significance:** Shifting cultivation has been practiced for centuries by indigenous communities, who rely on it for subsistence farming.
 
• **Government Initiatives:** Programs like the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) aim to provide support to farmers transitioning from Jhum cultivation to more sustainable methods.

questions.question: What provision was sanctioned by the Charter Act of 1813?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Introduction of western sciences**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Charter Act of 1813 allowed for the **promotion of Western education** in India, including sciences and literature.
 
• This act sanctioned a sum of **₹1 lakh annually** for the education of Indians to encourage the introduction of Western knowledge.
 
• The Act ended the monopoly of the East India Company in trade, except for trade in tea and trade with China, which indirectly supported the spread of education and knowledge.
 
• It laid the foundation for **modern education** in India by emphasizing the need for institutions to teach Western sciences and languages.
 
• Missionaries were allowed under the Act to propagate Christianity, which also contributed to the spread of English education in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1813**

 
 
• This Act was passed by the British Parliament to renew the charter of the East India Company.
 
• It marked a shift in British policy by introducing measures for the advancement of education in India.
 
• It also aimed to protect the rights of Indian subjects and bring changes in administrative governance.
 
 
 
• **Western Education in India**
 
 
• The Charter Act of 1813 was the first official step toward the establishment of English education in India.
 
• Western sciences and literature were introduced as part of a broader effort to modernize Indian education.
 
• It provided the groundwork for future educational reforms such as the Macaulay Minute of 1835.
 
 
 
• **Missionary Activities**
 
 
• The Act allowed Christian missionaries to enter India and propagate their religion.
 
• Missionaries were instrumental in establishing schools and colleges that taught Western sciences and languages.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Society**
 
 
• The introduction of Western sciences and literature helped Indians gain knowledge in various fields such as medicine, engineering, and law.
 
• It also contributed to the rise of a new educated middle class in India.

questions.question: Where was the 2024 International Conference of NGOs organised by UNESCO held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Paris, France**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2024 International Conference of NGOs under UNESCO was **organized in Paris, France**, where UNESCO’s headquarters are located.
 
• This conference is a biennial event that brings together UNESCO’s **official NGO partners** to discuss and align strategies for global development and cooperation.
 
• Paris has hosted numerous key UNESCO events, emphasizing its role as a global center for education, culture, and science.
 
• The conference primarily focuses on **strengthening collaboration between UNESCO and NGOs** to address global challenges like education, heritage preservation, and sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization)**

• Its headquarters is situated in **Paris, France**.

questions.question: Who has the authority to make laws for multi-state co-operative societies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The authority to make laws for multi-state co-operative societies is vested in the **Parliament of India**.
 
• Multi-state co-operative societies are governed by the **Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002**, which was enacted by Parliament.
 
• Multi-state co-operative societies operate in more than one state, and hence, come under the purview of the **Union List** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 246 of the Constitution assigns legislative powers over subjects in the Union List exclusively to Parliament.
 
• The Department of Co-operation, under the Ministry of Co-operation, oversees the implementation and regulation of laws concerning multi-state co-operative societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002:**

 
 
• It regulates the functioning of co-operative societies that operate across multiple states in India.
 
• The Act emphasizes democratic management, accountability, and transparency in co-operative societies.
 
• It provides provisions for registration, management, and dissolution of multi-state co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Union List:**
 
 
• The Union List is one of the three lists under the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It contains subjects on which only Parliament has the exclusive power to legislate.
 
• Examples include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and multi-state co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Co-operation:**
 
 
• Established in July 2021 to promote and strengthen co-operative societies across India.
 
• Its responsibilities include formulating policies and implementing programs related to co-operatives.
 
• The ministry also aims to streamline processes for multi-state co-operative societies.
 
 
 
• **Article 246 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Defines the distribution of legislative powers between Parliament and state legislatures.
 
• Subjects listed under the Union List are exclusively under Parliament’s jurisdiction.
 
• Co-operative societies operating across multiple states fall under Parliament's legislative domain due to their inclusion in the Union List.

questions.question: What is India's Human Development Index (HDI) value in the 2025 Human Development Index Report?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.685**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's Human Development Index (HDI) value for 2025 is projected to be **0.685**, as per the Human Development Index Report.
 
• The HDI is a composite index measuring average achievement in three basic dimensions of human development: **health, education, and standard of living**.
 
• India's HDI has been steadily improving due to consistent progress in **life expectancy, literacy rates, and per capita income**.
 
• India is classified as a country with **medium human development**, given its HDI value falls between 0.550 and 0.699.
 
• Despite improvements, India continues to face challenges such as **inequality, regional disparities, and low gender equality**, which impact its overall HDI ranking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**

 
 
• HDI is published annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in its Human Development Report.
 
• The index focuses on three dimensions: **health (life expectancy), education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (GNI per capita).**
 
• It ranges from 0 to 1, where a higher value indicates better human development outcomes.
 
 
 
• **India's HDI Trends**
 
 
• India's HDI value has seen consistent growth over the last few decades due to government initiatives in health, education, and poverty alleviation.
 
• For instance, India's HDI value was **0.645 in 2019**, and it has shown an upward trend despite challenges like the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
 
 
• **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)**
 
 
• IHDI accounts for inequality in the distribution of each dimension of HDI.
 
• India's IHDI value is typically lower than its HDI value, highlighting inequality in education, health, and income.
 
 
 
• **Global HDI Context**
 
 
• In the latest Human Development Report, countries like **Norway, Ireland, and Switzerland** rank highest in HDI.
 
• India's HDI ranking is typically around the **130-140 range**, reflecting its medium level of human development compared to global peers.

questions.question: During the colonial period, India's industrial development was the result of British policies. Which of the following options best describes the nature of industrial development in India at the eve of independence?

options.text: Balanced regional distribution of heavy industries
Strong domestic capital goods industry in all provinces
Widespread industrial growth across rural and urban areas
Limited industrial activity, mainly concentrated in a few cities like Calcutta and Bombay

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Limited industrial activity, mainly concentrated in a few cities like Calcutta and Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the colonial period, India's industrial development was largely limited due to the exploitative economic policies of the British government.
 
• Industrial activity was mainly concentrated in a few urban centers like Bombay (now Mumbai), Calcutta (now Kolkata), and Madras (now Chennai).
 
• Heavy industries and large-scale manufacturing units were almost absent, with small-scale industries such as textiles and jute dominating the industrial landscape.
 
• India's domestic capital goods industry was virtually non-existent, forcing reliance on imports from Britain.
 
• The rural areas of India were primarily agrarian, with little to no industrial activity, leading to regional imbalances in economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drain of Wealth Theory:** Proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji, it highlighted how colonial policies drained India's wealth to Britain, leaving limited resources for industrial development.
 
• **Deindustrialization:** The British systematically destroyed India's traditional handicrafts and small industries to promote British industrial goods, leading to widespread unemployment and poverty.
 
• **Economic Exploitation:** Colonial policies prioritized raw material exports (like cotton and jute) over domestic industrial growth, benefiting British industries at the expense of Indian economy.
 
• **Railways and Ports:** While infrastructure like railways and ports was developed, it primarily served colonial interests of transporting raw materials and finished goods rather than fostering industrial growth.
 
• **Post-Independence Scenario:** After independence, India focused on building a strong industrial base through initiatives like the Five-Year Plans and establishment of public sector enterprises.

questions.question: In applications with multiple tabs (like browsers or MS Word), what does Ctrl + Tab do?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Switches to the next tab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ctrl + Tab** is a commonly used keyboard shortcut to **switch to the next open tab** in applications that support multiple tabs, such as web browsers, code editors, and document processors.
 
• It cycles through tabs in the order they are listed, moving from left to right.
 
• This shortcut is universally recognized across major web browsers like **Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, and Safari**.
 
• In contrast, the shortcut **Ctrl + Shift + Tab** allows users to switch to the **previous tab** (from right to left).
 
• Using keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl + Tab significantly enhances productivity by eliminating the need to manually click on tabs with a mouse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts in Browsers:**

 
 
• **Ctrl + T**: Opens a new tab.
 
• **Ctrl + W**: Closes the current tab.
 
• **Ctrl + Shift + T**: Reopens the last closed tab.
 
• **Ctrl + 1 to Ctrl + 8**: Navigates directly to a specific tab (e.g., Ctrl + 1 goes to the first tab).
 
• **Ctrl + 9**: Jumps to the last tab, regardless of its position.
 
 
 
• **Tab Management in Applications:**
 
 
• Tabbed interfaces are widely used in software applications to improve **workflow and organization**.
 
• Examples include web browsers, text editors, and spreadsheet programs.
 
• Switching between tabs using shortcuts saves time, especially for power users who work with multiple tabs simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Other Useful Shortcuts:**
 
 
• **Alt + Tab**: Switches between open applications on Windows.
 
• **Cmd + Tab**: Switches between open applications on macOS.
 
• **Ctrl + F4**: Closes the current tab or window in applications.
 
 
 
• **Accessibility and Efficiency:**
 
 
• Keyboard shortcuts are designed to make computing faster and more **accessible** for all users.
 
• They reduce reliance on the mouse, which can be especially helpful for individuals with repetitive strain injuries.

questions.question: Which of the following authorities was strengthened in 2024 to enforce penalties and green clearances under India’s environmental regulations?

__
 
• In 2024, the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** was given enhanced powers to enforce penalties and ensure compliance with environmental regulations in India.
 
• The CPCB operates under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) and is the apex body for pollution control in the country.
 
• The amendments empowered the CPCB to impose stricter fines and oversee the implementation of green clearances to address environmental violations effectively.
 
• As part of its expanded role, the CPCB was tasked with ensuring adherence to environmental standards by industries, urban bodies, and other entities.
 
• The move aimed to strengthen India's capacity to tackle air, water, and soil pollution, ensuring sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB):**

• **Environmental Clearances in India:**
 
 
• Green clearances are required for activities that may have significant environmental impacts.
 
• These include projects in sectors like mining, infrastructure, and energy.
 
• The process is overseen by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) and the CPCB.

questions.question:

1. According to National Manufacturing Policy 2011, every job created in the manufacturing sector creates two-three additional jobs in related activities.

2. Industries add value to the existing goods and also to the skill of labour employed in it; therefore, this sector is also considered a transformational sector.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **National Manufacturing Policy 2011:** It highlights that every job created in the manufacturing sector leads to the creation of 2-3 additional jobs in related activities, emphasizing the multiplier effect of manufacturing employment.
 
• **Transformational Sector:** Industries add value to raw materials and enhance the skill set of workers, which is why the industrial sector is considered a transformational sector in economic development.
 
• **Employment & Poverty Eradication:** Industrial development plays a critical role in generating employment and is a precondition for eradicating poverty and unemployment in India.
 
• The industrial sector contributes significantly to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and serves as a backbone for the economic progress of the country.
 
• Policies like Make in India and National Manufacturing Policy aim to boost industrial growth and employment generation in India.

questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the principle of 'collective executive responsibility' as applicable to the Council of Ministers in India?

options.text: All ministers share full responsibility for government decisions.
Ministers can opt out of collective responsibility if they disagree publicly.
Only the Prime Minister is responsible for decision‑making.
Each minister is independent and is solely accountable for his/her actions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All ministers share full responsibility for government decisions.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Collective executive responsibility** is a principle enshrined in Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, which states that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
 
• This principle ensures that all members of the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, act as a single entity and take joint responsibility for the actions and policies of the government.
 
• If a decision is taken by the government, all ministers are expected to defend it publicly, even if they personally disagree with it.
 
• If a minister disagrees with a decision and is unwilling to defend it, the convention is that they must resign from their position.
 
• The principle of collective responsibility strengthens the unity of the executive and maintains the stability of the government by ensuring accountability to the legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 75(3):** This article specifies that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, ensuring that they act as a unified body in matters of governance.
 
• **Individual Responsibility:** While collective responsibility exists, each minister is also individually responsible for their respective departmental actions and policies.
 
• **No-Confidence Motion:** If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers, the entire Council, including the Prime Minister, is required to resign, demonstrating collective accountability.
 
• **Parliamentary Democracy:** The principle of collective responsibility is a cornerstone of parliamentary democracy, ensuring that the executive remains accountable to the legislature.
 
• **Westminster Model:** India’s collective responsibility principle is inspired by the Westminster model of governance, which emphasizes the unity and accountability of the executive branch.

questions.question: The Rashtrakutas dominated which part of India after the Guptas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rashtrakutas were a prominent dynasty that ruled large parts of the **Deccan region of India** from the 8th to 10th century CE.
 
• They established their capital at **Manyakheta (modern-day Malkhed in Karnataka)**.
 
• The Rashtrakutas were known for their patronage of art and architecture, most notably the **Kailasa temple at Ellora**, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• Under rulers like Amoghavarsha I, the Rashtrakutas achieved significant cultural, economic, and military prosperity in the Deccan region.
 
• Their empire extended over vast areas including parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rashtrakutas Origin:**

 
 
• The Rashtrakutas claimed descent from the Yadava lineage and were originally based in the Lattaluru region (modern-day Latur in Maharashtra).
 
 
 
• **Kailasa Temple:**
 
 
• This temple, carved out of a single rock, is considered an architectural marvel of the Rashtrakuta period.
 
• It reflects the technological and artistic prowess of ancient Indian artisans.
 
 
 
• **Amoghavarsha I:**
 
 
• One of the greatest Rashtrakuta rulers, he authored the Kannada classic *Kavirajamarga*.
 
• His reign marked the peak of Rashtrakuta cultural achievements.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Rashtrakutas:**
 
 
• The empire eventually fell to the Chalukyas of Kalyani in the late 10th century CE.
 
• Their decline marked the end of one of the most influential dynasties in the Deccan.

questions.question: Which of the following modern physicist closely examined Newtonian mechanics’ foundations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Albert Einstein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Albert Einstein critically examined the foundations of Newtonian mechanics and introduced revolutionary concepts that led to the development of modern physics.
 
• His theory of special relativity (1905) challenged Newtonian mechanics by introducing the constancy of the speed of light and the relativity of simultaneity.
 
• Einstein’s work revealed that Newtonian mechanics fails at speeds approaching the speed of light and in strong gravitational fields, leading to the development of general relativity (1915).
 
• The equivalence principle, a cornerstone of general relativity, contradicted Newton’s concept of absolute space and time.
 
• Einstein’s contributions fundamentally reshaped the understanding of space, time, and energy, pushing science beyond the classical framework established by Newton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newtonian Mechanics:**

 
 
• A classical physics framework developed by Sir Isaac Newton, describing motion using laws of inertia, force, and action-reaction.
 
• It assumes absolute space and time, which Einstein later challenged.
 
 
 
• **Special Relativity:**
 
 
• Developed by Albert Einstein in 1905, it introduced concepts like time dilation, length contraction, and E=mc².
 
• It applies to objects moving at constant speeds close to the speed of light.
 
 
 
• **General Relativity:**
 
 
• Published by Einstein in 1915, it describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
 
• It replaced Newton’s law of universal gravitation in explaining phenomena like black holes and cosmic expansion.
 
 
 
• **Equivalence Principle:**
 
 
• A concept in general relativity stating that gravitational force and acceleration are indistinguishable.
 
• It played a key role in Einstein’s departure from Newtonian mechanics.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Modern Physics:**
 
 
• Einstein’s work laid the foundation for quantum mechanics, cosmology, and advancements in theoretical physics.
 
• His discoveries opened new avenues in understanding the universe at both macroscopic and microscopic scales.

questions.question: Consider a computer system with a multi-core processor. What is the primary advantage of having multiple cores compared to a single-core processor with the same clock speed when executing multiple independent tasks simultaneously?

options.text: Increased capacity for the system's main memory (RAM)
Reduced power consumption for the overall system
Improved ability to handle and execute multiple separate processes concurrently
Enhanced speed for executing a single, heavily threaded application

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Improved ability to handle and execute multiple separate processes concurrently**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Multi-core processors allow multiple cores to work independently, enabling efficient execution of multiple independent tasks simultaneously.
 
• This architecture reduces bottlenecks caused by task switching in single-core systems, improving overall system performance.
 
• Each core operates as a separate processing unit, facilitating better multitasking and parallel processing capabilities.
 
• Multi-core systems are especially advantageous in environments requiring concurrent execution of multiple processes, such as servers or multimedia applications.
 
• While clock speed remains the same, multiple cores ensure more tasks are processed in parallel, leading to better utilization of system resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core:** A core is a processing unit within a CPU that performs computational tasks. Multi-core CPUs contain multiple cores in a single chip.
 
• **Parallel Processing:** The simultaneous execution of multiple processes or tasks by dividing them across multiple cores to improve efficiency.
 
• **Hyper-threading:** A technology used in some processors to enable a single core to handle multiple threads, though it does not replace the advantages of physical multi-core systems.
 
• **Single-core vs Multi-core:** Single-core processors execute one thread at a time, whereas multi-core processors can execute multiple threads or tasks concurrently.
 
• **Applications:** Multi-core processors are widely used in high-performance computing, gaming, video editing, and server systems requiring multitasking and parallel workloads.

questions.question: Under the reign of Islamic rulers, which among the following used to be a private building?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwan-i-Khas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Diwan-i-Khas** was a private hall used by Islamic rulers, specifically for confidential meetings and royal audiences.
 
• It served as a venue where the emperor met his ministers, nobles, and other important officials to discuss state affairs privately.
 
• The design of Diwan-i-Khas reflected grandeur and exclusivity, symbolizing the ruler’s authority and status.
 
• Famous examples of Diwan-i-Khas can be found in Mughal architecture, such as the Red Fort in Delhi and Fatehpur Sikri.
 
• Unlike Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), which was open to the general public, Diwan-i-Khas was highly restricted and accessible only to select individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarai**: Sarais were rest houses or inns constructed along trade routes to provide lodging and essential facilities to travelers, traders, and pilgrims.
 
• **Katra**: Katras were market complexes or caravanserais often used for commercial purposes. They were designed to accommodate traders and store goods.
 
• **Bridges**: Bridges constructed during the Islamic reign were primarily for public use, facilitating transportation and trade over rivers and other obstacles.
 
• **Diwan-i-Aam**: Unlike Diwan-i-Khas, the Diwan-i-Aam was a public hall where the emperor addressed grievances and petitions from common people.
 
• **Architectural Significance**: Structures like Diwan-i-Khas exemplify the blend of Persian, Islamic, and Indian architectural styles, showcasing intricate designs, inlaid marble work, and decorative arches.

questions.question: In February 2025, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs extended the deadline for private companies to dematerialise their securities. What is the new deadline?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 June 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)** in India extended the deadline for private companies to dematerialise their securities to **30 June 2025**.
 
• Dematerialisation is a process wherein physical certificates of securities are converted into electronic form.
 
• This extension was announced in February 2025 to provide private companies with adequate time to comply with regulations.
 
• The previous deadline for dematerialisation of securities was set earlier but has been extended for better implementation and compliance.
 
• Private companies are required to ensure their securities are held in electronic form through a depository participant registered with SEBI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dematerialisation of Securities:**

 
 
• Dematerialisation eliminates the risks associated with holding physical certificates, such as loss, theft, or forgery.
 
• Securities in electronic format are managed through depositories like NSDL (National Securities Depository Limited) and CDSL (Central Depository Services Limited).
 
• It facilitates easier transfer, trading, and monitoring of securities.
 
 
 
• **Depository Participant:**
 
 
• A Depository Participant (DP) acts as an intermediary between the investor and the depository.
 
• Registered with SEBI, DPs provide services like opening demat accounts, transferring securities, and holding securities electronically.
 
 
 
• **SEBI's Role:**

questions.question: What significant financial commitment was agreed upon during the extended session of COP16 in Rome?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the extended session of **COP16 **in **Rome**, member nations agreed to allocate **$200 billion annually** for biodiversity conservation.
 
• This financial commitment aims to address the ongoing global biodiversity crisis, including habitat loss, species extinction, and ecosystem degradation.
 
• The funding will support initiatives like **restoration of ecosystems, protection of endangered species**, and sustainable management of natural resources.
 
• The decision aligns with the objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) to protect 30% of the planet's land and marine areas by 2030, also known as the "30x30" target.
 
• Countries were encouraged to mobilize resources from both public and private sectors to meet this ambitious goal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):**

 
 
• An international treaty adopted in 1992 at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro.
 
• Aims to conserve biodiversity, promote sustainable use of its components, and ensure fair sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.
 
• The CBD has been ratified by 196 nations, making it a globally recognized framework for biodiversity protection.
 
 
 
• **30x30 Target:**
 
 
• A global initiative to protect at least 30% of Earth's land and ocean areas by 2030.
 
• Proposed under the Global Biodiversity Framework to halt and reverse biodiversity loss.
 
• Focuses on safeguarding key biodiversity hotspots and ecosystems critical for climate regulation.
 
 
 
• **Global Biodiversity Crisis:**
 
 
• According to the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES), over 1 million species are at risk of extinction.
 
• Major drivers include deforestation, climate change, pollution, and overexploitation of natural resources.
 
• Urgent action is necessary to prevent irreversible damage to ecosystems and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanisms:**
 
 
• Countries are urged to mobilize financial resources through mechanisms like green bonds, biodiversity trust funds, and public-private partnerships.
 
• International organizations like the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and Green Climate Fund (GCF) play a pivotal role in financing biodiversity initiatives.

questions.question: In the balanced reaction 2Al + 3Cl₂ → 2AlCl₃, what is the mole ratio of aluminium to aluminium chloride?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: 2 : 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is: **2Al + 3Cl₂ → 2AlCl₃**.
 
• In the reaction, **two moles of aluminium (Al)** react with **three moles of chlorine gas (Cl₂)** to produce **two moles of aluminium chloride (AlCl₃).**
 
• The mole ratio of aluminium (Al) to aluminium chloride (AlCl₃) is **2:2**, which simplifies to **1:1**.
 
• This ratio indicates that for every two moles of aluminium, two moles of aluminium chloride are formed.
 
• The correct option is **Option 1: 2 : 2**, as it directly reflects the stoichiometric coefficients in the balanced equation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stoichiometry**: The branch of chemistry that deals with the quantitative relationships between reactants and products in a chemical reaction.
 
• **Mole Ratio**: Derived from the coefficients of the balanced chemical equation and represents the proportional relationship between substances involved in the reaction.
 
• **Balanced Equation**: Ensures the conservation of mass, where the number of atoms for each element is the same on both sides of the equation.
 
• **Reaction Details**: Aluminium reacts with chlorine gas to form aluminium chloride, an ionic compound commonly used in chemical synthesis and industrial processes.
 
• **Limiting Reactant Concept**: In practical scenarios, the reactant present in a lower stoichiometric quantity may limit the amount of product formed, but this does not affect the mole ratio derived from the balanced equation.

• This socio-religious movement was led by **Jadonang and later Rani Gaidinliu** with the aim of reviving Naga traditions and customs.
 
• The movement also sought to oppose British colonial rule and Christian missionary influence in the region.

• It led by Chittur Singh and Umaji Naik, was a response to British annexation policies in the Western Ghats.
 
• The Ramosis were a tribal community employed as hill police during Maratha rule but were marginalized under British rule.
 
 
 
• **Lushai Revolt**
 
 
• This revolt occurred in the **present-day Mizoram (then part of Assam)** during the 19th century.
 
• The Lushai tribes resisted British interference in their territory and culture.
 
• The British eventually subdued the rebellion and brought the region under their control.
 
 
 
• **Kol Rebellion**

• The rebellion was led by the Kol tribal community against exploitative landlords and moneylenders.
 
• It was a significant tribal uprising during British colonial rule.

• After his execution by the British, **Rani Gaidinliu** became the leader and continued the fight for Naga identity and freedom.
 
• Rani Gaidinliu is remembered as a freedom fighter and was posthumously awarded the **Padma Bhushan**.

questions.question: Which plateau lies between the Aravali and the Vindhya Range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Malwa Plateau is located in the central part of India and lies **between the Aravali and Vindhya ranges**.
 
• It is primarily spread across the states of **Madhya Pradesh** and **Rajasthan**, with some portions extending into Gujarat.
 
• The plateau is characterized by **black soil**, which is highly fertile and suitable for agriculture, particularly for crops like wheat, cotton, and soybean.
 
• This region is also known for its geological significance, being a part of the **Deccan Traps**, which are made up of volcanic basalt rock.
 
• Key rivers such as the **Chambal, Kali Sindh, and Parbati** originate or flow through the Malwa Plateau, enriching the region's agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aravali Range:**

 
 
• One of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, running diagonally across Rajasthan and parts of Haryana and Gujarat.
 
• It acts as a natural barrier, influencing the climate and biodiversity of the region.
 
 
 
• **Vindhya Range:**
 
 
• A mountain range running parallel to the Narmada River, forming the southern boundary of the Malwa Plateau.
 
• It is geologically younger than the Aravali range and influences the northern boundary of the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Traps:**
 
 
• A large igneous province in west-central India, formed due to volcanic activity around 66 million years ago.
 
• The basaltic rock formations contribute to the region's black soil, which is ideal for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Key Cities:**
 
 
• Important cities located in the Malwa Plateau include **Indore, Ujjain, Ratlam, and Neemuch**.
 
• Ujjain is a major religious and cultural hub, known for the **Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• The plateau is rich in mineral resources like limestone and is a hub for cement production.
 
• It also plays a crucial role in agriculture, being one of the most fertile regions in central India.

• **Output Devices:**

questions.question: What is another name for the Great Himalayan range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inner Himalayas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Inner Himalayas, also referred to as the Great Himalayan Range, are the **highest mountain range in the Himalayas**.
 
• This range contains some of the world's tallest peaks, including **Mount Everest (8,849m)**, Kanchenjunga (8,586m), and Nanga Parbat (8,126m).
 
• The Great Himalayan range serves as a natural boundary between the Indian subcontinent and the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• It spans across five countries: **India, Nepal, Bhutan, China, and Pakistan**, making it a significant geographical feature of South Asia.
 
• It is characterized by **perpetual snow cover, glaciers, and alpine vegetation**, contributing to its ecological and hydrological significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shiwalik Range**

 
 
• The Shiwalik Range, also known as the Outer Himalayas, is the **lowest and southernmost range of the Himalayas**.
 
• It is composed of unconsolidated sediments like sandstone and conglomerates, making it prone to erosion.
 
• The elevation of the Shiwalik Range typically varies from **600 to 1,200 meters above sea level**.
 
• It forms a transition zone between the plains and the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Central Axial Range**
 
 
• This term is not commonly used to describe the Great Himalayan range but may refer to the central spine of the Himalayan region.
 
• It generally includes peaks from the Inner Himalayas like Everest and Kanchenjunga.
 
 
 
• **Northeastern Hills**
 
 
• The Northeastern Hills are a distinct geographical region in India, located in the northeastern states such as Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, and Meghalaya.
 
• They are not part of the Great Himalayan Range but are a separate geological formation.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance of the Inner Himalayas**
 
 
• The Inner Himalayas act as a **source of perennial rivers** such as the Ganges, Indus, and Brahmaputra, vital for agriculture and human settlements.
 
• The range supports a variety of flora and fauna, including endangered species like the snow leopard and red panda.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **regulating climate** and maintaining biodiversity in the region.

questions.question: Which Hindustani music style has originated from the folk songs of the camel-riders of North-West India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tappa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tappa** is a **semi-classical style of Hindustani music** that originated from the folk songs sung by camel riders in North-West India, particularly in Punjab.
 
• The word "**Tappa**" means "**jump**" or "**leap**," reflecting the fast, intricate, and rhythmic nature of this music style.
 
• Tappa is characterized by its highly ornamented and rapid musical phrases known as "**taan**" and "**gamak**."
 
• The style was popularized by **Ghulam Nabi Shori**, also known as "**Shori Miyan**," during the 18th century in the court of Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula of Awadh.
 
• Tappa compositions often express themes of love and longing and are performed in languages such as Punjabi and Urdu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Classical Music:**

 
 
• Hindustani classical music is one of the two main traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• It originated in North India and is based on the system of "**ragas**" (melodic framework) and "**taals**" (rhythmic cycles).
 
• It incorporates elements of Persian and Mughal influences along with indigenous Indian traditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Hindustani Styles:**
 
 
• **Dhrupad:** The oldest style of Hindustani vocal music, characterized by its solemn and meditative nature.
 
• **Thumri:** A romantic and lyrical form of semi-classical music often associated with themes of love and devotion.
 
• **Khayal:** A more modern and improvisational style of Hindustani classical music that emphasizes creativity and emotional expression.
 
 
 
• **Gamak and Taan:**
 
 
• **Gamak:** Ornamentation in Indian classical music that involves oscillating or shaking notes.
 
• **Taan:** Fast, intricate melodic patterns that showcase the performer's virtuosity.
 
 
 
• **Regional Influence:**
 
 
• Tappa's roots lie in the folk traditions of camel riders from Punjab and North-West India.
 
• Its lyrics are often in regional languages, making it accessible and relatable to local audiences.

questions.question: What is the primary reason that roughage is included in a balanced human diet?

• Roughage, also known as dietary fiber, is essential for **maintaining healthy bowel movements** by adding bulk to stool and preventing constipation.
 
• It promotes the growth of **healthy gut bacteria**, which aids digestion and supports overall gut health.
 
• Roughage helps in **regulating blood sugar levels** by slowing down the absorption of glucose in the bloodstream.
 
• Including adequate fiber in the diet reduces the risk of **digestive disorders**, such as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).

• **Types of Dietary Fiber:**

 
 
• **Soluble fiber:** Dissolves in water and forms a gel-like substance, helping to lower cholesterol and glucose levels. Found in oats, fruits, and legumes.
 
• **Insoluble fiber:** Does not dissolve in water and aids in adding bulk to stool, preventing constipation. Found in whole grains, nuts, and vegetables.
 
 
 
• **Recommended Intake:** The daily recommended intake of dietary fiber is **25 grams for women** and **38 grams for men**, as per dietary guidelines.
 
• **Health Benefits:** Fiber-rich foods help in reducing the risk of chronic diseases such as **type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and colorectal cancer**.
 
• **Sources of Roughage:** Common sources include **whole grains, fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds, and legumes**.

questions.question: In its advisory capacity, the Union Cabinet’s advice to the President of India is considered:

options.text: overruled by the Speaker of the Lower House

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**binding to the President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Cabinet's advice to the President of India is **binding under Article 74(1) of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The President is constitutionally obligated to act in accordance with the advice provided by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• This principle emphasizes the concept of a parliamentary democracy where the President functions as a nominal head, while real executive power resides with the Council of Ministers.
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 made it explicit that the President "shall act in accordance with such advice."
 
• Although the President may initially return advice for reconsideration, if the same advice is sent back, the President is bound to accept it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 74(1):** This article states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, and the President shall act in accordance with such advice.
 
• **42nd Amendment Act (1976):** This amendment explicitly made the President's compliance with the advice of the Council of Ministers mandatory, strengthening the parliamentary system of governance.
 
• **Reconsideration Power:** While the President can send a recommendation back to the Council of Ministers for reconsideration, once the advice is reiterated, it becomes binding.
 
• **Nominal vs. Real Executive:** The President is the nominal executive head, while the Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister, exercises real executive authority.
 
• **Parliamentary Democracy:** India follows a parliamentary system of governance where the President acts as the constitutional head, and the Council of Ministers is responsible to the Parliament.
